content.title: About
content.content: Catfish fillet is the flesh of a freshwater catfish, prepared by deep‑frying. The fish has a firm, white meat with a mild flavor that becomes richer when fried. It is commonly served as steaks, strips, or bite‑size pieces coated in breadcrumbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Catfish can grow over a meter long, but culinary uses usually involve younger, smaller specimens.
In many countries (e.g., the United States, Russia, and China) catfish is a popular fast‑food item and is often featured in fish‑and‑chips style dishes.
High‑heat frying creates a crispy crust while preserving most of the protein and essential amino acids.
Compared with many other fried fish products, catfish has relatively low fat content when lightly breaded.
Traditional Southeast Asian cuisines often marinate catfish in spices before frying.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Catfish provides about 18–20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and helps maintain a healthy immune response.

items.title: Low mercury levels
items.content: Unlike many marine fish, catfish typically contains low levels of mercury, making it safer for frequent consumption.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Small amounts of omega‑3 fatty acids in catfish can help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to catfish.

items.title: Calorie‑dense
items.content: Deep‑frying adds significant calories and fat, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Catfish raised in polluted waters may contain heavy metals; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can create trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Catfish fillets are typically deep‑fried in vegetable oil until golden brown. Serve with lemon wedges, tartar sauce, fresh salads, or in a sandwich. For a lighter option, bake in the oven with a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fried catfish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
